item.title: Five Hundred Billion Tokens to Reverse-Engineer a Classic Shooter
item.description: Autonomous agents spent months chewing through half a trillion tokens to decompile a legacy first-person shooter, revealing that surface-level progress masked deep semantic corruption. The project exposes a sobering engineering bottleneck: code generation is cheap, but enforcing rigorous semantic correctness without human drift remains an open problem.

item.title: A plastic once thought harmless may be fueling fatty liver disease
AI agents in a stand-up call
Talorys Runs a Personal Agent on Cloudflare's Free Tier
item.description: Talorys repackages local agent infrastructure onto serverless edge primitives, offering a self-hosted architecture that bypasses recurring subscription models. The central tradeoff remains the operational overhead of managing edge bindings and state persistence manually.

item.title: Veda: The First Agentic Hobby Operating System
Political Capital Secures a Billion-Dollar Compute Pipeline
item.description: Tom Brown leveraged Washington connections to broker a massive monthly SpaceX compute allocation, illustrating how infrastructure scarcity increasingly bows to political leverage rather than engineering merit. The arrangement accelerates private compute centralization while bypassing open market accountability.

item.title: Trading One Black Box for Another
item.description: The flood of AI-generated scientific data delivers answers and artifacts without the underlying human understanding or proofs required to decode them, shifting our challenge from discovery to comprehension. Quote: We’ve traded one black box for another, and still need to unpack it.

item.title: Anthropic Revises Terms to Prohibit Sustained Cruelty Toward Claude
item.description: Anthropic updated its usage policy to ban prolonged, purposeless abuse directed at its language models, leaning on Claude's built-in capability to terminate hostile conversations. While engineered primarily to prevent training feedback loops and curb toxic human habits, the mandate awkwardly brushes against unresolved questions surrounding machine personhood.
